raw_text:
Thank you — below is a progressive 12‑week postpartum return-to-exercise programme tailored to a 33‑year‑old female, 4 weeks post uncomplicated C‑section, cleared for light activity only (walking, no abdominal exercise, no heavy lifting until six‑week check). It assumes training at home with only a yoga mat. The plan is conservative, prioritizes pelvic floor and diastasis recti protection, gradual reintroduction of strength and core work after the six‑week OB check, and includes recovery and nutrition guidance.

Important safety notes (read first)
- Continue to follow the OB’s advice. If at any point she experiences new or worsening pain, a bulge, coning in the midline, heaviness in the pelvic floor, urinary leakage, or increased bleeding, stop exercise and consult her OB/physio.
- No resisted abdominal (‘crunching’) or heavy lifting until OB clears at ~6 weeks. Start gentle core/pelvic floor retraining only if no contraindications and ideally with input from a pelvic health physiotherapist (strongly recommended).
- Progress only if symptoms are well tolerated (no increased bleeding, pain, heaviness, or pelvic floor symptoms).
- Keep intensity light for weeks 4–6; from week 7 onward progress cautiously according to symptom response.

Overview: phases
- Weeks 1–2 of programme (Client weeks 4–5 postpartum): Recovery + mobility + walking; pelvic floor awareness only, no abdominal loading.
- Weeks 3–4 of programme (Postpartum weeks 6–7): After six‑week check and clearance — begin low-load strength, gentle core re‑education, continued walking and mobility.
- Weeks 5–8 of programme (Postpartum weeks 8–11): Build strength, introduce progressive bodyweight resistance, low‑impact cardio, and controlled core work.
- Weeks 9–12 of programme (Postpartum weeks 12–15): Increase intensity and functional strength, further core progression, introduce more dynamic movements as tolerated.

Structure per week
- 3 structured sessions per week (approx. 20–40 minutes depending on phase) plus daily walking and mobility; flexibility to swap session days. Rest days/active recovery between strength sessions.
- Each session includes breathing/pelvic floor cueing and a short cool-down.

Weeks 1–2 (Postpartum weeks 4–5) — Goals: gentle movement, walking base, pelvic floor awareness, scar mobility (if cleared), sleep/convalescence support
Frequency: daily low‑intensity walking (5–20 minutes) + 3 mini home sessions per week (20–25 min)

General guidance (every session)
- Diaphragmatic breathing and gentle pelvic floor awareness: 3–5 minutes seated or supine. Encourage gentle inhale to soften belly, exhale to feel slight pelvic floor and low‑abdominal engagement without bearing down. No Valsalva, no crunching.
- Avoid any bilateral heavy lifting (baby lifting okay with an upright posture and using legs, bracing gently).

Session A (x1 per week)
- Warm up: 5 minute easy walk + shoulder rolls, neck turns.
- Pelvic floor/diaphragmatic breathing: 5 minutes. Cue: inhale belly out slightly, exhale engage pelvic floor lightly (a gentle lift, not a strong squeeze).
- Strength/mobility circuit — 2 rounds, rest 60–90s between rounds:
  1) Seated/standing heel raises — 12–15 reps (slow)
  2) Glute squeezes (lying supine, knees bent) — 10–12 reps, hold 2–3s
  3) Cat–cow on all fours — 8–10 slow reps
  4) Standing hip abduction (side leg lift) — 8–12 reps per side
- Cool down: gentle hamstring and calf stretch, 1–2 minutes.

Session B (x1 per week)
- Warm up: 5 minute brisk walk
- Pelvic floor cueing: 3 minutes (standing).
- Mobility/activation — 2 rounds:
  1) Marching in place (lift knees to comfortable height) — 60s
  2) Bridge hold gently (pelvic tilt to lift hips a few inches) — 8–10 reps, 2–3s hold
  3) Quadruped rocking (on hands/knees, rock back toward heels) — 8–10 reps
  4) Wall push‑ups (standing) — 8–12 reps
- Cool down: breathing and gentle pelvic floor relaxation.

Session C (x1 per week)
- Light yoga-based mobility (20–25 min): child’s pose, gentle seated twist (avoid deep abdominal compression), supine knee hugs, gentle side-lying hip work. Finish with 3–5 minutes breathing.

Daily walking: start at 5–10 minutes twice daily at conversational pace; progress to 20 minutes total over week 2 as tolerated.

Weeks 3–4 (Postpartum weeks 6–7) — Goals: after six‑week check (assume cleared for light strengthening), begin low‑load strength, introduce gentle core retraining and standing functional movements
Frequency: 3 structured sessions per week, walking 20–30 min most days

General rules
- Begin gentle core reconnecting: pelvic floor activation + transversus abdominis (TVA) draw-in/abdominal hollowing done gently in standing/seated positions. Avoid traditional crunches, bilateral straight leg raises, or heavy Valsalva.
- Start with bodyweight multi‑joint exercises, higher repetitions, slow tempo.
- Continue scar mobilization (if cleared; gentle circular friction around scar after 6 weeks only if healed and advised).

Week structure (repeat each week for 2 weeks)

Session 1 — Strength lower‑body emphasis (25–35 min)
- Warm up: 5–7 min walk + hips/ankle mobility
- Breathing + pelvic floor cue: 3–4 min (standing)
- Circuit 3 rounds, rest 60–90s:
  1) Supported squat to chair (sit to stand) — 10–12 reps
  2) Glute bridge (partial to full range as tolerated) — 10–12 reps
  3) Split stance hip hinge (bodyweight Romanian deadlift, hands on chair) — 8–10 per side
  4) Side‑lying clamshells — 12–15 per side
- Cool down + gentle stretches

Session 2 — Upper body & posterior chain (25–35 min)
- Warm up: brisk 5 min walk, shoulder circles
- Circuit 3 rounds:
  1) Incline/wall push‑ups — 8–12
  2) Bent‑over row with water bottles (hip hinge, light weight) — 10–12
  3) Bird‑dog (alternating, focus on neutral spine) — 8–10 per side
  4) Standing single‑arm carry simulation (hold a baby doll or book) — 20–30s per side focusing on posture
- Finish with breathing and pelvic floor relaxation.

Session 3 — Mobility + light core retraining (20–30 min)
- Warm up: 5 min walk
- Gentle TVA draw‑in progressions:
  1) Seated TVA activation — 3 sets of 8–10 breaths (hold the gentle draw for 4–5s each)
  2) Seated marching with TVA engaged — 2 sets 30s
  3) Modified side plank from knees (only if no diastasis coning; very gentle) — 8–12s holds x3 per side
- Hip mobility: 2 rounds of kneeling lunge-to-hip flexor stretch (30s each)
- Cool down.

Walking: 20–30 min most days at moderate pace as tolerated.

Weeks 5–8 (Postpartum weeks 8–11) — Goals: progressive strength, introduce more core work, increase walking/cardio volume
Frequency: 3 strength sessions per week, 3–4 walking/cardio sessions (20–35 min)

Progression principles
- Increase load by adding household weights (water bottles, backpack with books) or increasing reps/sets.
- Continue pelvic floor and TVA cues for all strength moves. Avoid breath-holding.

Week-by-week outline (Weeks 5–6 then Weeks 7–8 increase difficulty)

Weeks 5–6 (Sessions moderate)
Session A — Full-body strength (35–40 min)
- Warm up: 7 min brisk walk + mobility
- Circuit 3 rounds:
  1) Goblet squat with light weight (water bottle/book) — 10–12
  2) Glute bridge single‑leg progressions (start bilateral, progress to unilateral as tolerated) — 8–10 per side
  3) Bent‑over row (dumbbells/water bottles) — 10–12
  4) Standing single‑leg RDL to touch — 8–10 per side
- Core finisher (gentle): 2 sets — dead bug progression (arms/legs march, maintaining TVA) 8–10 slow reps per side
- Cool down.

Session B — Upper focus + posterior chain
- Warm up
- 3 rounds:
  1) Incline push‑ups or regular push-ups from knees — 8–12
  2) Superman hold (prone) — 8–10 x 3s
  3) Seated/standing shoulder press with light weight — 10–12
  4) Lateral band/weight step‑outs or side band walks — 10–15 per side
- Cool down.

Session C — Movement + low‑impact cardio
- 20–30 min walk or gentle interval walk (1–2 min faster/2–3 min easy)
- Mobility + pelvic floor work (5–7 min)

Weeks 7–8 (Increase challenge)
- Increase sets to 3–4, slightly heavier household weights, or add extra walking time.
- Add unilateral work and progress dead bug to more limbs extended as tolerated (only when no coning).
- Introduce short bouts of gentle core loading: standing Pallof press with band (anti‑rotation) 8–12 per side.

Weeks 9–12 (Postpartum weeks 12–15) — Goals: build strength, endurance, functional capacity; reintroduce more dynamic activity if asymptomatic
Frequency: 3 structured strength sessions + 1–2 cardio sessions per week

Progression and safety
- By week 9–12, if no diastasis recti symptoms and pelvic floor is strong, incorporate more dynamic core moves (plank progressions, side planks, controlled lower abdominal loading). Still avoid maximal Valsalva and heavy loads unless cleared.
- Consider referral to pelvic health physiotherapist for higher‑level core rehabilitation if needed.

Sample weekly progression (Weeks 9–12) — increase intensity each two weeks

Session 1 — Strength (lower focus)
- Warm up 7–10 min
- 4 rounds:
  1) Split squat (rear foot elevated optional) — 8–10 per side
  2) Hip thrust (single leg progressions) — 8–10
  3) Step‑ups with weight — 8–12 per side
  4) Farmer carry (backpack filled) — 40–60s
- Core: Modified plank (on elbows/knees progress to toes) 3 x 20–45s as tolerated.

Session 2 — Strength (upper focus)
- Warm up
- 4 rounds:
  1) Push‑up progression — 8–15
  2) Single‑arm row — 10–12 per side
  3) Overhead press — 8–12
  4) Band‑or‑weight pull‑apart — 12–15
- Core: Pallof press 3 x 10 per side.

Session 3 — Full-body + conditioning
- Warm up
- Circuit 3–4 rounds:
  1) Squat jumps or squat to calf raise (low impact if needed) — 8–12
  2) Reverse lunge with rotation (light) — 8 per side
  3) Mountain climbers slow controlled (30s) — only if pelvic floor tolerates
  4) Bent‑over row — 10–12
- Finish with 20–30 min brisk walk or light jog intervals only if pelvic floor OK.

Return to running or high-impact: Only attempt if pelvic floor symptoms absent and cleared by clinician; introduce gradually using run/walk method.

Nutrition, recovery and general advice
- Calories: support breastfeeding if applicable — approx. add 300–500 kcal/day above pre‑pregnancy needs while breastfeeding. If not breastfeeding, aim for a modest calorie deficit only after cleared and when weight loss is a goal. Encourage whole foods, balanced macronutrients.
- Protein: aim for ~1.2–1.6 g/kg bodyweight per day to support recovery and muscle rebuilding.
- Hydration: frequent fluid intake, especially if breastfeeding.
- Iron: screen for anemia symptoms (fatigue, lightheadedness). Encourage iron‑rich foods and follow OB guidance on supplementation.
- Sleep: prioritize short naps and shared caregiving when possible; sleep is critical for recovery — reduce training intensity on low‑sleep days.
- Pelvic floor: perform gentle pelvic floor activations daily (3–5 short squeezes, 3–5 longer holds within comfortable limits) — but avoid over‑training the pelvic floor.
- Scar care: after incision fully healed and cleared (often 6 weeks+), gentle scar massage may reduce adhesions and sensitivity; follow OB/physio guidance.
- Follow‑up: strongly recommend a pelvic health physiotherapist assessment around 8–12 weeks for objective diastasis recti and pelvic floor evaluation to guide further progressions (return to heavy lifting or running).

Red flags — stop and consult:
- New or worsening pelvic pain, heaviness, bulging/coning in the midline, increased urinary/fecal leakage, increased bleeding, fever, or increased abdominal pain.

Example 12‑week calendar summary (concise)
- Weeks 1–2: Short walks, 3 gentle sessions/week focusing on pelvic floor awareness, glute activation, mobility.
- Weeks 3–4: Post‑6‑week check: start low‑load strength (bodyweight), standing TVA work, continue walking.
- Weeks 5–6: Progress load/reps, introduce small household weights, dead bug progressions.
- Weeks 7–8: Add unilateral work, anti‑rotation core (Pallof), increase walking/cardio.
- Weeks 9–10: Increase intensity and volume of strength sessions, begin plank progressions if no symptoms.
- Weeks 11–12: More dynamic/functional work, conditioning, prepare for return to normal fitness routine as tolerated. Refer to pelvic physio before heavy lifting.

- Provide specific example progressions for core rehabilitation for diastasis recti (with photos or video links).
- Tailor calorie and macronutrient targets if you give current weight, height, breastfeeding status and goals.
